message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This workflow will install Python dependencies, run tests and lint with a variety of Python versions
# For more information see: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/automating-builds-and-tests/building-and-testing-python

name: Python package

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "main" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "main" ]

jobs:
  build:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13", "3.14"]

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-python@v7
      with:
        python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
    - name: Cache pip dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/pip
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        python -m pip install pytest
        pip install .
    - name: Run tests
      run: |
        pytest",
  "rationale": "The repository runs a Python test matrix across six versions and installs dependencies (pytest and the package from pyproject.toml) on every run. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern and the matching measured experiment (batch-hiruni) show adding an actions/cache@v4 step for ~/.cache/pip keyed on hashFiles('pyproject.toml') with restore-keys, placed after setup-python and before dependency installation. pyproject.toml exists in the repository and CI history shows repeated runs, so repeated pip fetching is measurable. The cache only stores dependency downloads; it does not change installation, tests, or required checks, so build/test coverage is preserved. No permissions are weakened and no new network access, secrets, or deployment operations are added.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
